mainTopic: Stories of righteous people with spiritual power, and of fasts for rain answered through humility, good deeds and leadership.
overview: The amud opens with a short exchange. רבי יוסי בר אבין suggests a detail to רב אשי about שמואל's rule on pulling a fish from the water on שבת, and then reveals that he himself is the author of that detail. He explains that he left his teacher, רבי יוסי דמן יוקרת, because that teacher had no mercy even on his own children. The גמרא then tells how that teacher decreed early death for his son, who made a fig tree give fruit out of season. He did the same to his beautiful daughter, who was causing people to sin. It adds a story about his donkey, which would carry home only its exact rental fee. Next comes אלעזר איש בירתא, who gave his daughter's dowry money to orphans. His granary was then miraculously filled, but he made the wheat הקדש for his own family. The גמרא returns to fasts for rain: רבי יהודה נשיאה and רב נחמן bring rain through a broken heart. אושעיא warns that the leaders are the 'eyes' of the generation, and רבי יוחנן rules that individuals are drawn after a public fast. אילפא and a teacher of young children bring rain through their quiet good deeds. Finally, people ask רבה why his fast fails when רב יהודה's did not, and his answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: שמואל's ruling about a fish pulled from the sea on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר אבין overhears רב אשי learning a statement of שמואל: pulling a fish out of the sea on שבת makes one liable once a סלע-sized spot on it has dried.
steps.simpleTranslation: One day he heard him learning: שמואל said, if someone pulls a fish out of the sea on שבת, once a spot the size of a סלע coin has dried on it, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new story by telling us that רבי יוסי בר אבין overheard רב אשי reviewing a halacha of שמואל. That halacha sets up the conversation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A fish taken out of water slowly dies, and killing a living creature is a forbidden מלאכה on שבת. שמואל says that once a סלע-sized area of its skin dries, the fish can no longer survive. At that point the person is already חייב, even if he throws the fish back.

keyTerms.meaning: One who pulls out or draws up
A coin; used here as a measure of size
Liable, meaning he is guilty of breaking שבת

phrases.english: One day he heard him studying,
phrases.notes: From the story just before this, the listener is רבי יוסי בר אבין and the one learning is רב אשי.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
One who pulls a fish out of the sea on Shabbat,
once a spot on it the size of a sela coin has dried —
phrases.notes: A dry spot that big means the fish can't survive anymore, so in effect he has killed it.

phrases.english: he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הַשּׁוֹלֶה דָּג מִן הַיָּם בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pulling a fish from the water on שבת makes one liable once a סלע-sized area of it has dried.

steps.title: Adding the detail 'between its fins'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר אבין tells רב אשי that he should add that the dry spot must be between the fins.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Let the Master also say, 'and between its fins'!
steps.whatsHappening: The listener interrupts and suggests a more exact version of שמואל's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He is not rejecting שמואל. He is pointing out that the version רב אשי recited is missing a detail. Only a dry spot in the area between the fins makes the fish unable to survive.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the Master say; a polite way of suggesting a correction

phrases.english: He said to him:
Then let the Master say: "and between its fins"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the rule quoted in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of שמואל's rule as רב אשי recited it
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule as recited is too broad. The drying only counts when it is between the fins.

steps.title: רב אשי asks whose addition that is
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks whether the speaker doesn't know that this addition comes from רבי יוסי בן רבי אבין.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Doesn't the Master hold that רבי יוסי בן רבי אבין said that?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers with a question. He asks why the 'between its fins' detail was not said in the name of רבי יוסי בן רבי אבין, who said it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי is asking why the detail was not said in the name of its author, רבי יוסי בן רבי אבין, since whoever says a thing in the name of its author brings redemption to the world. He does not realize he is speaking to that very Sage.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Doesn't the Master hold

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָהִיא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן רַבִּי אָבִין אַמְרַהּ?
phrases.english: that Rabbi Yosei ben Rabbi Avin said that one?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the speaker knows that the addition belongs to רבי יוסי בן רבי אבין.

steps.title: 'I am he'
steps.stepSummary: The speaker reveals that he himself is רבי יוסי בר אבין.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I am he.
steps.whatsHappening: The surprise of the story: the man correcting רב אשי is the author of the addition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains why he knew the detail so well. It also shows that רבי יוסי בר אבין is now in רב אשי's study hall, which leads to the next question.

phrases.english: He said to him: I am he.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The speaker is רבי יוסי בר אבין himself.

steps.title: Weren't you a student of רבי יוסי דמן יוקרת?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks whether he used to learn with רבי יוסי דמן יוקרת, and he says yes.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Didn't the Master used to be found before רבי יוסי of יוקרת? He said: Yes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי checks a fact about רבי יוסי בר אבין's past. This sets up the real question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once רב אשי knows who he is, he recalls that this Sage studied under רבי יוסי דמן יוקרת. The 'yes' confirms it, so רב אשי can now ask why he left.

keyTerms.meaning: Before him; learning in front of a teacher

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: וְלָאו קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי דְּמִן יוֹקֶרֶת
phrases.english: Wasn't it before Rabbi Yosei of Yokrat
that the Master was regularly found?
He said to him: Yes.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָאו קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי דְּמִן יוֹקֶרֶת
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יוסי בר אבין had studied under רבי יוסי דמן יוקרת (answer: yes).

steps.title: Why did you leave him?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks why he left his teacher and came here.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: And why did the Master leave him and come here?
steps.whatsHappening: Now רב אשי asks the main question: why did this student switch study halls?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving one's רב was a serious step, so רב אשי wants to know the reason. The answer will move the גמרא toward the stories about רבי יוסי דמן יוקרת.

phrases.english: He said to him:
And what is the reason the Master left him
and came here?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason רבי יוסי בר אבין left רבי יוסי דמן יוקרת.

steps.title: A man with no mercy on his own children
steps.stepSummary: He explains that his teacher had no mercy even on his own son and daughter, so he would not have mercy on a student.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: A man who had no mercy on his son or on his daughter, how would he have mercy on me?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בר אבין explains that he left out of fear of his teacher's extreme strictness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He argues from the greater case to the lesser one. If the teacher was harsh with his own children, he would surely be harsh with a student. The mention of the son and daughter sets up the stories the גמרא will tell next.

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: גַּבְרָא דְּעַל בְּרֵיהּ וְעַל בְּרַתֵּיה לָא חָס,
phrases.english: A man who had no mercy on his son or on his daughter,
how would he have mercy on me?!

steps.triggerLanguage: גַּבְרָא דְּעַל בְּרֵיהּ וְעַל בְּרַתֵּיה לָא חָס
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He left because his teacher was so strict that he spared not even his own children.

steps.title: What happened with his son?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the story with the son was.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the story with his son?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the story behind the claim about the son. This is a setup line that opens the story coming next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim in step 7 needs proof. The גמרא is about to tell the incident that shows the teacher's harshness.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? What is the story?

phrases.english: His son, what is that story?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The incident showing the harshness of רבי יוסי דמן יוקרת toward his son.

steps.title: The son makes the fig tree give fruit
steps.stepSummary: The father's hired workers were hungry and he was late with their food, so the son commanded a fig tree to give fruit, and it did.
steps.simpleTranslation: One day he hired workers in the field. It got late and he did not bring them bread. They told his son, 'We are starving!' They were sitting under a fig tree. He said, 'Fig tree, fig tree, bring out your fruit so my father's workers can eat.' It produced fruit and they ate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins the story of the son. Out of kindness, he uses his spiritual power to feed his father's hungry workers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The son's motive is good: he does not want the workers to suffer. But he gets food by changing nature, making the tree give fruit out of season. That is exactly what the father will object to.

phrases.english: One day there were, hired by him,
workers in the field,

phrases.aramaic: נְגַהּ לְהוּ וְלָא אַיְיתִי לְהוּ רִיפְתָּא,
phrases.english: it got late for them and he did not bring them bread,
they said to his son: We are starving!
They were sitting under a fig tree,
he said: Fig tree, fig tree!
Bring out your fruit,
so that my father's workers may eat.
It brought out fruit, and they ate.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹמָא חַד הֲווֹ אֲגִרִי לֵיהּ אֲגִירֵי בְּדַבְרָא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The son made a fig tree bear fruit to feed the hungry workers.

steps.title: The father arrives and learns what happened
steps.stepSummary: The father arrives, apologizes for being late because he was busy with a מצוה, and the workers tell him his son already fed them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Meanwhile the father came and said to them: Don't hold it against me. I was late because I was busy with a מצוה, and I was on the road until now. They said: May the Merciful One satisfy you as your son satisfied us. He asked: From where? They told him what had happened.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. The father finds out about the miracle, which sets up his harsh reaction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father had a good reason for being late, since he was busy with a מצוה. The workers bless him with thanks, but when he asks how his son fed them, he learns about the miracle.

phrases.english: Meanwhile, his father came,
he said to them: Don't hold it against me,
for the fact that I am late,
I was busy with a מצוה,
and I was on my way until just now.
They said to him:
May the Merciful One satisfy you
just as your son satisfied us.
He said to them: From where?
phrases.notes: He means: where did my son get food to give you?

phrases.english: They said: Such and such was what happened.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The father learns that his son fed the workers through a miracle.

steps.title: The father's harsh response: 'You will be taken before your time'
steps.stepSummary: The father tells his son that because he troubled his Creator to make the fig tree give fruit before its time, he will be taken before his time.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: My son, you troubled your Creator to make a fig tree bring out its fruit not in its time. You will be taken not in your time.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with the father's punishment of his son. This proves רבי יוסי בר אבין's point that this teacher had no mercy even on his own son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father's complaint is not that the son fed the workers. It is that he 'troubled' ה׳ to change nature for a small need. The punishment matches the act: the tree gave fruit before its time, so the son will die before his time.

keyTerms.meaning: You troubled, you put to effort
Will be gathered in, meaning will die

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי בר אבין left רבי יוסי דמן יוקרת because of his extreme strictness. The proof is that he even said his own son would die young for troubling ה׳ with a miracle out of season.
steps.confusionAlert: The son did nothing selfish; he fed hungry workers. The father's anger is about using a miracle to change nature for something that could have waited, not about the kindness itself.

phrases.english: He said to him: My son,
you troubled your Creator
to make a fig tree bring out its fruit not in its time —
may he be gathered in not in his time.
phrases.notes: 'Gathered in' means passing away. The son died young, measure for measure with the early fruit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the son's story and proves the claim made in step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוסי דמן יוקרת was so strict that he said his own son would die before his time for troubling ה׳ with an out-of-season miracle. This confirms why his student left him.

steps.title: What was the story with his daughter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the story of the daughter, which was mentioned earlier.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the story of his daughter?
steps.whatsHappening: The student said earlier that his teacher had no mercy on his son or his daughter. We already heard the son's story, so now the גמרא asks for the daughter's story. This line sets up the story that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches the earlier question about the son (step 8). The student's claim covered two people, so the גמרא fills in the second example.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? (asking for the details of a story)

phrases.english: His daughter, what is [the story]?
phrases.notes: This goes back to step 7, where the student said his teacher had no mercy on his son or his daughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the son's story, the גמרא now asks about the second person mentioned in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What happened with רבי יוסי דמן יוקרת's daughter that showed he had no mercy on her.

steps.title: A man peeks at the beautiful daughter through a hedge
steps.stepSummary: The daughter was very beautiful, and one day her father saw a man making a hole in the hedge to look at her.
steps.simpleTranslation: He had a beautiful daughter. One day he saw a certain man making a hole in the hedge and looking at her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts answering the question: it describes the daughter and the man who was peeking at her. This sets up the conversation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her beauty is presented as the root of the problem: it was leading people to look at her in an improper way. The hole in the hedge shows how far this man was willing to go to see her.

keyTerms.meaning: A hedge or fence made of branches

phrases.english: He had a beautiful daughter.
One day he saw a certain man
who was piercing a hole in the hedge
and was looking at her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12 by beginning the daughter's story.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The daughter was very beautiful, and a man was caught peeking at her through a hole in the hedge.

steps.title: The man explains why he was looking
steps.stepSummary: The father asks the man what he is doing. The man answers that if he can't marry her, he should at least get to look at her.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What is this? The man answered: My teacher, if I didn't merit to marry her, shall I not even merit to look at her?
steps.whatsHappening: The father confronts the man, and the man defends himself. His answer sets up the father's reaction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man is not ashamed; he thinks looking is a small consolation. His answer shows the father that his daughter's beauty is causing other people to stumble.

phrases.english: He said to him: What is this?
He said to him: My teacher,
if I did not merit to take her [in marriage],
shall I not merit to [at least] look at her?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: the father confronts the man he saw in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The man justifies his peeking: since he can't marry her, he wants at least to look at her.

steps.title: The father tells his daughter to return to her dust
steps.stepSummary: The father tells his daughter that she is causing people distress, so she should return to her dust and people will no longer stumble because of her.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to her: My daughter, you are causing people pain. Return to your dust, and let people not stumble into sin because of you.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of the daughter's story: the father decrees that she should leave this world. This proves the student's claim that his teacher had no mercy even on his own daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This mirrors the son's story (step 11), where the father also decreed his child's death. The reason here is different: the daughter was not doing anything wrong, but her beauty was making other people sin.

keyTerms.meaning: You are causing pain or distress

steps.whatToRemember: Both stories, the son and the daughter, show how strict רבי יוסי דמן יוקרת was. That is why his student said a teacher like that would surely not have mercy on a student.

phrases.english: He said to her: My daughter,
you are causing distress to people.
Return to your dust,
and let people not stumble because of you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The father reacts to the man's answer in step 14 and ends the daughter's story.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוסי דמן יוקרת decreed his daughter's death so that people would not sin because of her. This completes the proof that he had no mercy even on his own children.

steps.title: The donkey that brought home its exact fee
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי דמן יוקרת had a donkey that was rented out every day. In the evening it came home with the exact fee on its back, and it refused to come if the amount was too much or too little.
steps.simpleTranslation: He had a certain donkey. People rented it every day, and in the evening they sent it back with its rental money on its back, and it would go to its owner's house. If they added to the money or took some away, it would not go.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells another story about רבי יוסי דמן יוקרת: even his donkey was miraculously careful about money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The donkey would only carry exactly what was owed: no more and no less. The story shows how honest and exact its owner was.

phrases.english: He had a certain donkey.
When people would hire it each day,
in the evening they would send it back
with its fee on its back,
and it would come to its owner's house.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי טָפוּ לַהּ אוֹ בָּצְרִי לַהּ —
phrases.english: But if they added to it or took away from it,
phrases.notes: This refers to the money: if the fee was more or less than what was owed.

phrases.english: it would not come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the stories about his children, the גמרא adds another story about the same חכם, this time about his donkey.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי's donkey miraculously carried home only its exact rental fee, and it refused to move if the amount was wrong.

steps.title: The donkey refuses to carry forgotten sandals
steps.stepSummary: One day someone forgot a pair of sandals on the donkey, and it would not go until the sandals were taken off.
steps.simpleTranslation: One day they forgot a pair of sandals on it, and it did not go until they took them off. Then it went.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives an example of the donkey's exactness: even something left there by accident stopped it from going home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody meant to give extra here; the sandals were simply forgotten. Even so, the donkey would not bring home anything that did not belong to its owner, so the story shows how careful it was.

phrases.aramaic: יוֹמָא חַד אִינְּשׁוֹ זוּגָא דְסַנְדָּלֵי עֲלַהּ,
phrases.english: One day they forgot a pair of sandals on it,
and it did not go until they took them off it,
and then it went.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹמָא חַד אִינְּשׁוֹ זוּגָא דְסַנְדָּלֵי עֲלַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a specific example of the donkey's behavior that was described in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even forgotten sandals stopped the donkey until they were removed.

steps.title: The צדקה collectors hide from אלעזר איש בירתא
steps.stepSummary: The צדקה collectors used to hide from אלעזר איש בירתא, because he gave them everything he had. One day he was going to buy his daughter's dowry, and they hid from him again.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whenever the charity collectors saw אלעזר איש בירתא, they hid from him, because he would give them everything he had with him. One day he was going up to the market to buy a dowry for his daughter. The charity collectors saw him and hid from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story about a different צדיק, אלעזר איש בירתא, known for being extremely generous. This step sets up the scene for what he does next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually people avoid the צדקה collectors, but here the collectors avoid the giver, so that he won't give away everything. On this day there was even more reason to hide, because he needed the money for his daughter's dowry.

keyTerms.meaning: A dowry (what a bride brings into her marriage)

phrases.english: Elazar of Birta:

phrases.aramaic: כַּד הֲווֹ חָזוּ לֵיהּ גַּבָּאֵי צְדָקָה
phrases.english: when the charity collectors would see him,
they would hide from him,

phrases.aramaic: דְּכׇל מַאי דַּהֲוָה גַּבֵּיהּ יָהֵיב לְהוּ.
phrases.english: because whatever he had with him he would give them.
One day he was going up to the market
to buy a dowry for his daughter.
The charity collectors saw him and hid from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא moves from רבי יוסי דמן יוקרת to a new story about a different צדיק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אלעזר איש בירתא was so generous that the צדקה collectors hid from him, even on the day he was buying his daughter's dowry.

steps.title: אלעזר chases the collectors and asks what they are collecting for
steps.stepSummary: אלעזר runs after the collectors and makes them swear to tell him what they are collecting for. They say it is for an orphan boy and an orphan girl.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went and ran after them and said: I make you swear, what are you busy with? They told him: With an orphan boy and an orphan girl.
steps.whatsHappening: Instead of being glad they hid, אלעזר chases them down to find out what מצוה they are collecting for. Their answer sets up his decision in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He chases them even though he is on the way to buy his own daughter's dowry. The answer, an orphan couple, is very close to his own situation: they need money to get married too.

keyTerms.meaning: I make you swear (I adjure you)
You are busy with / involved in
An orphan boy and an orphan girl

phrases.english: He went and ran after them.
He said to them: I make you swear [to tell me]:
What are you busy with?
They said to him: With an orphan boy and an orphan girl.
phrases.notes: They mean they are collecting money so the two orphans can marry each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: אלעזר will not let the collectors avoid him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The collectors were raising money for the wedding of an orphan boy and an orphan girl.

steps.title: אלעזר gives away his daughter's dowry money
steps.stepSummary: אלעזר swears that the orphans come before his own daughter and gives them everything he has. With his last זוז he buys wheat and throws it into his storehouse.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I swear by the Temple service that they come before my daughter. He took everything he had with him and gave it to them. He was left with one זוז; he bought himself wheat, brought it up, and threw it into the granary.
steps.whatsHappening: אלעזר puts the orphans' wedding ahead of his own daughter's and gives them almost all his money. The story is not over yet: the wheat in the granary sets up what happens next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He swears that the orphans' wedding comes before his own daughter's, even though he was on his way to buy her dowry. He keeps only one coin, buys a little wheat, and puts it in storage. This small detail is the setup for the miracle that the גמרא tells next.

keyTerms.meaning: By the Temple service (a way of making an oath)
A granary, a storehouse for grain

steps.whyThisMatters: This story shows real self-sacrifice for צדקה, especially for orphans getting married. It also sets up the reward that comes in the continuation of the story.

phrases.english: He said to them: [I swear] by the Temple service
that they come before my daughter.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁקַל כֹּל דַּהֲוָה בַּהֲדֵיהּ וִיהַב לְהוּ.
phrases.english: He took everything he had with him and gave it to them.
He was left with one zuz;
he bought himself wheat,
and brought it up and threw it into the granary.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: הָעֲבוֹדָה שֶׁהֵן קוֹדְמִין לְבִתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the collectors' answer in step 19 by giving them his daughter's dowry money.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אלעזר swore that the orphans came before his daughter, gave them everything, and put wheat bought with his last זוז into his granary.

steps.title: The wife asks what her husband brought home
steps.stepSummary: אלעזר's wife asks their daughter what her father brought for the dowry. The daughter says he threw everything he brought into the storehouse.
steps.simpleTranslation: His wife came and asked her daughter: What did your father bring? The daughter answered: Whatever he brought, he threw into the storehouse.
steps.whatsHappening: The story of אלעזר איש בירתא goes on. His wife wants to know what he bought for their daughter's wedding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the last step אלעזר spent his last זוז on a little wheat and threw it into the storehouse. This conversation sets up the surprise that comes next. As far as the family knows, there is almost nothing in there.

phrases.english: His wife came
she said to her daughter:
What did your father bring?
She said to her:
Whatever he brought, he threw into the storehouse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story right after אלעזר threw his small amount of wheat into the storehouse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The family thinks the storehouse holds only the little wheat that אלעזר bought.

steps.title: The storehouse is miraculously full of wheat
steps.stepSummary: The wife goes to open the storehouse. It is so packed with wheat that grain spills out of the door's socket and the door will not open.
steps.simpleTranslation: She went to open the door of the storehouse. She saw that it was full of wheat, which was coming out through the door's socket, and the door would not open because of all the wheat.
steps.whatsHappening: A miracle happens. The tiny amount of wheat has become a storehouse filled past the top.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אלעזר gave away everything for the orphans and kept almost nothing for himself. Now his storehouse is overflowing. The story shows heaven repaying his generosity many times over.

keyTerms.meaning: The socket the door turns in

phrases.english: She came to open the door of the storehouse,
she saw the storehouse full of wheat
and it was coming out through the socket of the door,
and the door would not open because of the wheat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows what was really inside the storehouse the daughter mentioned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The storehouse was miraculously filled with wheat.

steps.title: אלעזר makes the miracle wheat הקדש for his daughter
steps.stepSummary: The daughter runs to the בית מדרש to tell her father about the miracle. He swears that the wheat is הקדש as far as she is concerned, so she may take only what any poor person in ישראל could take.
steps.simpleTranslation: His daughter went to the בית מדרש and said to him: Come and see what the One Who loves you has done for you! He said to her: By the Temple service, this wheat is הקדש as far as you are concerned, and you have no share in it except like one of the poor of ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: אלעזר hears about the miracle and refuses to let his family get special benefit from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of enjoying the gift, אלעזר declares it הקדש. His daughter can have only the share any poor person would get. He does not want to profit for himself from a miracle, and that ends the story.

keyTerms.meaning: By the Temple service, a form of oath
Property set aside as holy, which may not be used for oneself

steps.whatToRemember: אלעזר איש בירתא gave everything to צדקה. When a miracle repaid him, he still would not let his own family take more than any poor person could.

phrases.english: His daughter went to the study hall,
she said to him:

phrases.aramaic: בֹּא וּרְאֵה מָה עָשָׂה לְךָ אוֹהַבְךָ!
phrases.english: Come and see what the One Who loves you has done for you!
He said to her: By the Temple service,
they are הקדש as far as you are concerned,
and you have no share in them
except like one of the poor of Israel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives אלעזר's reaction to the miracle and closes the story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אלעזר makes the wheat הקדש toward his daughter and gives her only a poor person's share.

steps.title: רבי יהודה נשיאה's broken heart brings rain
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה נשיאה decreed a fast, but no rain came. He compared himself to שמואל הנביא and cried out about his generation. He felt crushed, and then rain came.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה נשיאה decreed a fast and prayed, but rain did not come. He said: How great is the difference between שמואל of רמה and יהודה בן גמליאל! Woe to the generation that is stuck with this, and woe to the one in whose days this happened! He felt crushed, and rain came.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its main subject, fasts for rain, with a new story about the נשיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His prayer did not work at first. He blamed himself as a weak leader compared to שמואל, whose prayer brought rain even in summer. His humility and broken heart are what brought the rain.

keyTerms.meaning: שמואל הנביא, from the town of רמה

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda Nesia decreed a fast,
he prayed for mercy, and rain did not come.
He said: How great is the difference between Samuel of Ramah
and Yehuda ben Gamliel!
Woe to the generation that is stuck with this,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹי לוֹ לְמִי שֶׁעָלְתָה בְּיָמָיו כָּךְ!
phrases.english: woe to the one in whose days this happened!
He felt crushed, and rain came.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אלעזר story and returns to the theme of fasting for rain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain came only after the נשיא felt broken and humbled.

steps.title: ריש לקיש worries that they did not accept the fast the night before
steps.stepSummary: The נשיא's household decreed a fast but told רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש only in the morning. ריש לקיש points out that they never accepted the fast the evening before.
steps.simpleTranslation: The house of the נשיא decreed a fast and did not tell רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש. In the morning they told them. ריש לקיש said to רבי יוחנן: But we did not accept it upon ourselves the evening before!
steps.whatsHappening: A new story raises a practical question about fasting. This step sets up the problem, and רבי יוחנן answers it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a fast counts only if a person accepts it upon himself the day before. They heard about this fast only in the morning, so ריש לקיש asks whether it can count for them.
steps.confusionAlert: ריש לקיש is not refusing to fast. He is raising the rule that a fast has to be accepted ahead of time, and asking whether this fast can count.

phrases.english: The house of the Nasi decreed a fast,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אוֹדְעִינְהוּ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וּלְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ.
phrases.english: and they did not inform Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish.
In the morning they informed them.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said to Rabbi Yochanan:
But we did not accept it upon ourselves from the evening!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another story about a fast decreed by the נשיא, this time raising a halachic issue.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a public fast count for someone who did not accept it the evening before?

steps.title: We are pulled along after the community
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that individuals are drawn after the community, so a public fast counts even without accepting it the night before.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We are drawn after them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers ריש לקיש's worry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A public fast decreed by the נשיא binds everyone automatically. Each person is part of the community's fast, so he does not need to accept it on his own.

keyTerms.meaning: We are drawn or pulled along

steps.whatToRemember: For a public fast, an individual does not need to accept it the day before. He is pulled along with the community.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical rule. Accepting a fast ahead of time is needed only for a private fast, not for a fast decreed for the whole community.

phrases.english: He said to him:
We are drawn after them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ריש לקיש's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A public fast covers individuals automatically because they are drawn after the community.

steps.title: אושעיא quotes the פסוק about the 'eyes of the congregation'
steps.stepSummary: Another fast by the נשיא's household brings no rain. אושעיא, the youngest of the group, quotes a פסוק calling the leaders the 'eyes of the congregation.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The house of the נשיא decreed a fast, and rain did not come. אושעיא, the youngest of the group, taught them: 'And it shall be, if it was done in error from the eyes of the congregation.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new story starts with a failed fast. אושעיא quotes a פסוק, and the גמרא is setting up a teaching that will be explained in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of the 'eyes of the congregation,' meaning its leaders. By quoting it, אושעיא is hinting that the lack of rain is connected to the leadership, the 'eyes' of the people. The full point comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: The eyes of the congregation, meaning its leaders

phrases.english: The house of the Nasi decreed a fast
and rain did not come.

phrases.aramaic: תְּנָא לְהוּ אוֹשַׁעְיָא זְעֵירָא דְּמִן חַבְרַיָּיא:
phrases.english: Oshaya, the youngest of the group, taught them:
"And it shall be, if from the eyes of the congregation
it was done in error."

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנָא לְהוּ אוֹשַׁעְיָא זְעֵירָא דְּמִן חַבְרַיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story about a fast by the נשיא that failed to bring rain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אושעיא brings a פסוק that calls the leaders the 'eyes of the congregation,' setting up a lesson about leadership.

steps.title: The parable of the bride's eyes
steps.stepSummary: אושעיא compares the generation to a bride. If her eyes are beautiful, the rest of her surely is too. If her eyes are bleary, her whole body needs checking.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like a bride in her father's house. As long as her eyes are beautiful, her whole body does not need to be checked. If her eyes are bleary, her whole body needs to be checked.
steps.whatsHappening: אושעיא finishes his point from the last step with a parable. If the leaders, the 'eyes' of the community, are flawed, the whole community is suspect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 27 he quoted a פסוק calling the leaders the 'eyes of the congregation.' Now he explains why that matters. The eyes show what the whole body is like, so flawed leaders are a sign that the whole generation is unworthy. He is hinting that the rain was held back because of the נשיא's household.

phrases.english: A parable: a bride who is in her father's house.
As long as her eyes are beautiful,
her whole body does not need to be examined.
If her eyes are bleary,
her whole body needs to be examined.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes אושעיא's statement from step 27 with an explaining parable.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The leaders show the condition of the whole generation. If they are flawed, the whole generation is suspect.

steps.title: The servants mistreat אושעיא and his townspeople defend him
steps.stepSummary: The נשיא's servants put a scarf around אושעיא's neck and torment him. His townspeople tell them to leave him alone, because everything he does is for the sake of Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: His servants came, put a scarf around his neck, and were tormenting him. The people of his town said to them: Leave him alone. He hurts us too with his sharp criticism. But since we see that everything he does is for the sake of Heaven, we say nothing to him and let him be. You should let him be too.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: the נשיא's servants punish אושעיא for insulting the household. His neighbors step in and defend him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The townspeople admit that אושעיא's criticism is painful. Still, they put up with it because his motives are pure, לשם שמים. They ask the servants to treat him the same way.

phrases.aramaic: אֲתוֹ עַבְדֵּיהּ וּרְמוֹ לֵיהּ סוּדָרָא בְּצַוְּארֵיהּ,
phrases.english: His servants came and put a scarf around his neck,
phrases.notes: 'His servants' means the נשיא's servants, and 'his neck' is אושעיא's neck.

phrases.english: and they were tormenting him.
The people of his town said to them:
Leave him alone, because he hurts us too.

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דַּחֲזֵינַן דְּכׇל מִילֵּיהּ לְשׁוּם שָׁמַיִם,
phrases.english: Since we see that everything he does is for the sake of Heaven,

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָמְרִינַן לֵיהּ מִידֵּי וְשָׁבְקִינַן לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: we say nothing to him and let him be.
You should let him be too.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתוֹ עַבְדֵּיהּ וּרְמוֹ לֵיהּ סוּדָרָא בְּצַוְּארֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells how people reacted to אושעיא's criticism and closes the story of the נשיא's household.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Painful criticism is put up with when it is clearly said for the sake of Heaven.
steps.whatToRemember: This closes the stories about the נשיא's household. The leaders' behavior affects the whole generation, and sincere criticism said לשם שמים should be tolerated.

steps.title: אילפא's prayer brings rain at once
steps.stepSummary: רבי decrees a fast, but no rain comes. אילפא leads the prayers. When he says 'משיב הרוח' the wind blows, and when he says 'מוריד הגשם' the rain comes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי decreed a fast, but rain did not come. אילפא went down before him to lead the prayers (some say it was רבי אילפי). He said 'Who makes the wind blow,' and the wind blew. He said 'Who makes the rain fall,' and the rain came.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story about a fast. רבי's own fast did not bring rain, but when אילפא led the prayers, his words were answered immediately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even רבי, the great leader, could not bring rain with his fast. But אילפא's words came true one after another, wind and then rain. This sets up the question of what made him so special.

keyTerms.meaning: went down before him (to lead the prayers)
Who makes the wind blow (a line in שמונה עשרה)

phrases.english: רבי decreed a fast
but rain did not come.
אילפא went down before him to lead the prayers
(and some say it was רבי אילפי),
he said 'Who makes the wind blow,' and the wind blew,
'Who makes the rain fall,' and the rain came.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי גְּזַר תַּעֲנִיתָא וְלָא אֲתָא מִיטְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about prayers for rain that are answered.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When אילפא led the prayers at רבי's fast, his prayer for rain was answered right away.

steps.title: רבי asks about his good deeds
steps.stepSummary: רבי asks אילפא what good deeds earned him such a quick answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What are your deeds?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי asks a question to find out the reason for the miracle. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumes that a quick answer to prayer comes from some special merit. רבי wants to know what that merit is.

phrases.english: He said to him: What are your deeds?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the reason for the miracle in step 30.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What merit made אילפא's prayer work so quickly.

steps.title: Bringing wine for קידוש and הבדלה to a poor town
steps.stepSummary: אילפא explains that he lives in a poor town with no wine. He goes to the trouble of bringing wine so the people can fulfill קידוש and הבדלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I live in a poor town that has no wine for קידוש and הבדלה. I go to the trouble of bringing wine for קידוש and הבדלה, and I make them fulfill their obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: אילפא answers רבי's question and names his special מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His merit is helping a whole town keep קידוש and הבדלה, which they could not do without him. He takes on real effort for the public, and that is what made his prayer so powerful.

phrases.english: He said to him: I live in a poor town
that has no wine for קידוש and הבדלה.
I go to the trouble and bring
phrases.notes: The printed גמרא says 'and I come' (in round brackets), but the corrected wording, in square brackets, is 'and I bring.'

phrases.english: wine for קידוש and הבדלה,
and I make them fulfill their obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: His merit is bringing wine to a poor town so everyone can fulfill קידוש and הבדלה.

steps.title: In רב's town, a prayer leader brings rain
steps.stepSummary: רב comes to a certain place and decrees a fast, but no rain comes. The prayer leader says 'משיב הרוח' and the wind blows, then 'מוריד הגשם' and the rain comes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב came to a certain place. He decreed a fast, but rain did not come. The prayer leader went down before him. He said 'Who makes the wind blow,' and the wind blew. He said 'Who makes the rain fall,' and the rain came.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second story just like the first, this time with רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern repeats: a great leader's fast doesn't work, but an unknown prayer leader's words bring wind and rain. This sets up the question about his merit.

phrases.english: רב happened to come to a certain place,
he decreed a fast, but rain did not come.
The prayer leader went down before him,
he said 'Who makes the wind blow,' and the wind blew,
he said 'Who makes the rain fall,' and the rain came.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story that follows the same pattern as step 30.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Another ordinary prayer leader's prayer for rain is answered right away.

steps.title: רב asks about his good deeds
steps.stepSummary: רב asks the prayer leader what good deeds he does.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What are your deeds?
steps.whatsHappening: רב asks the same question רבי asked in the first story. This sets up the prayer leader's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא repeats the exact question on purpose, to show that the second story works just like the first. Again, the quick answer to prayer is traced back to a merit.

phrases.english: He said to him: What are your deeds?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the reason for the miracle in step 33.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What merit made this prayer leader's prayer work.

steps.title: The teacher who teaches poor children free and coaxes them to learn
steps.stepSummary: The prayer leader is a teacher of young children. He teaches poor children just like rich ones and takes no money from those who can't pay. He uses fish from his pond to coax children who don't want to learn.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I am a teacher of young children. I teach the children of the poor just like the children of the rich. Whoever can't afford it, I take nothing from him. I have a fishpond, and any child who slacks off, I win him over with the fish. We calm him and soothe him until he comes and reads.
steps.whatsHappening: The prayer leader answers רב and describes how he teaches children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His merit has three parts. He gives poor children the same teaching as rich ones, he doesn't charge those who can't pay, and he gently draws in children who resist learning. His caring dedication to teaching Torah is what brought the rain.

phrases.english: He said to him: I am a teacher of young children,
and I teach the children of the poor just like the children of the rich.
And whoever can't afford it,
I take nothing from him.
And I have a fishpond,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל מַאן דְּפָשַׁע מְשַׁחֵידְנָא לֵיהּ מִינַּיְיהוּ,
phrases.english: and any child who slacks off, I win him over with them,
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the fish. He uses them as a treat to coax the child back to learning.

phrases.english: and we calm him and soothe him
until he comes and reads.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 34.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He teaches poor children like rich ones, takes no money from those who can't pay, and gently coaxes reluctant children to learn.
steps.whatToRemember: In both stories, the great leader's fast is not enough. The prayer that brings rain comes from the one leading the prayers, and his merit is a quiet, steady habit of helping others: wine for a poor town, or Torah for poor and struggling children.

steps.title: רב נחמן's fast fails until he is humbled
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן declares a fast and no rain comes. He speaks harshly about himself, becomes heartbroken, and then the rain comes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן declared a fast and prayed, but no rain came. He said: 'Take נחמן and throw him off the wall to the ground!' He became heartbroken, and the rain came.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells another short story about a fast for rain. Here, רב נחמן's broken heart is what brings the rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last two stories showed rain coming because of someone's good deeds. This story goes back to the pattern of רבי יהודה נשיאה in step 24. רב נחמן's prayer alone did not work, but once he felt truly crushed and humbled (חלש דעתיה), the rain came.

keyTerms.meaning: he became upset or heartbroken (literally, 'his mind grew weak')

steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is not giving an order to other people. He is speaking about himself in the third person, out of pain that his fast did not work.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman decreed a fast,
he prayed for mercy, but rain did not come.
He said: Take Nachman,
phrases.notes: He's talking about himself, as if to say: 'This נחמן's fast was worthless.'

phrases.english: and throw him from the wall to the ground.
He grew upset, and rain came.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another story to the series about fasts for rain. Unlike the two stories just before it, the rain comes through a broken heart, as in the story of רבי יהודה נשיאה in step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sincerely broken and humbled heart can bring an answer when prayer alone did not.

steps.title: רבה's fast fails and people compare him to רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבה declares a fast with no result. People point out that when רב יהודה declared a fast, rain did come.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה declared a fast and prayed, but no rain came. People said to him: 'But when רב יהודה declared a fast, rain came!'
steps.whatsHappening: Another fast fails, and the people challenge רבה by comparing him to an earlier leader. This sets up רבה's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people assume that a great leader's fast should bring rain. So they ask why רבה, who is also a great leader, has less success than רב יהודה did.

keyTerms.meaning: 'but isn't it so that...' (introduces a challenge)
when he would (something that happened regularly)

phrases.english: Rabba decreed a fast.
He prayed for mercy, but rain did not come.
They said to him: But Rav Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲוָה גָּזַר תַּעֲנִיתָא אֲתָא מִיטְרָא.
phrases.english: when he would decree a fast, rain would come!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story. Unlike the last one, it turns into a discussion of why later generations' fasts are less effective.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's standing as a leader whose fast should bring rain
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רב יהודה's fasts worked, why don't רבה's? This implies something is lacking in רבה or his generation.

steps.title: רבה begins: our generation is greater in Torah learning
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that he cannot do anything about it. If the difference were Torah learning, his generation is actually superior, since in רב יהודה's years all their learning was... (the sentence continues on the next amud).
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: 'What can I do? If it is about Torah learning, we are greater than them. For in the years of רב יהודה, all of their learning...'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה begins to answer the challenge. He rules out Torah learning as the reason his fast failed. His sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה argues that the difference cannot be about Torah learning, because his generation learns more broadly than רב יהודה's did. This sets up the real explanation, which the גמרא will give next.

phrases.english: He said to them: What can I do?
If it is because of Torah learning,
we are superior to them,
for in the years of Rav Yehuda, all of their learning

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the comparison to רב יהודה by first rejecting Torah learning as the reason.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rules out one possible explanation before giving the real one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבה's fast failed because his generation learns less Torah than רב יהודה's did.
steps.terutzMaskana: Torah learning is not the reason, since רבה's generation is greater in learning. The real reason is still to come.
